name: Conduct due diligence on direct private equity investments
summary: A direct private equity deal team takes an opportunity that passed screening into deep, second-round diligence, usually in a seller's auction and alongside a sponsor or other partners. The team reviews the data room, meets management, builds the financial model, hires accounting, strategy, legal and environmental advisers, and gets tax, sustainability and value creation input. About half of these deals end with an investment memo sent to Risk and the Portfolio Execution Committee; the rest are dropped on red flags or price or lost in the auction. The seller's timetable compresses the work, adviser reports and internal inputs arrive late, and memos go through several rounds of edits.

baseline.org_archetype: A very large Canadian national pension fund manager whose private equity department invests directly in companies alongside sponsors, with internal deal teams and outside advisers.
baseline.notes: Covers phase 2 (deep) diligence from screening approval to memo submission. Tax structuring, ESG assessment, risk review, committee approval and closing are separate processes.

trigger: The group head accepts a screening memo and the team is invited into the second round of a sale process or a partner invites the fund into a bilateral deal.
end_state: An investment memo is submitted to Risk and the Portfolio Execution Committee, or the deal is dropped or lost.

volume.seasonality: Fewer deals in the first half of fiscal 2021 during the pandemic; busy in late calendar 2021.

evidence.note: Process map volume derived from the deal funnel (23.7 of 100 opportunities reach deep diligence). Likely high for direct PE alone: DPE added a net 3 investments in F2021 (85 to 88).
Group head leads go or no-go calls and partner negotiations. Role in phase 2 deal work; FTE is the author's estimate from hands-on time per deal times 28 deals a month.

roles.title: Associate, PE portfolio and business management
roles.department: PE strategy, portfolio and business management

evidence.note: Business management associate checks authority level and memo completeness; estimate from common practice.

systems.name: Deal pipeline and relationship management system
Virtual data rooms run by sellers and advisors
Bloomberg terminals, market data and trade messaging
Document management and investment committee memo repository
Compliance system for personal trading, attestations and restricted lists

steps.name: Staff deal team and set the phase 2 workplan
steps.description: After the group head accepts the screening memo, the director names the principal, associates and analyst, sets the phase 2 timetable against the seller's process letter, drafts an adviser budget and logs the deal stage in the pipeline system.

evidence.note: Phase 2 kick-off follows the first-round bid in an auction. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct or co-control deal.

steps.name: Clear conflicts and add target to the watch list
steps.description: A compliance officer checks the target and its lenders against existing holdings and the restricted list, adds the target to the watch list in the compliance system and confirms the information barrier before the team receives non-public data.

control.basis: Code of Conduct and confidential information policy: watch and restricted list entry before receiving material non-public information

evidence.note: Common institutional practice for confidential deal information; the organisation's restricted list appears in its process map. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct or co-control deal.

steps.name: Request proposals and engage outside advisers
steps.description: The principal asks accounting, strategy, legal and environmental firms for scope and fee proposals, compares them, negotiates caps and signs engagement letters within the deal's approved transaction cost budget.

error.defect_description: Scope misses a workstream such as IT, pensions or a foreign subsidiary.

control.basis: Expense management policy with seniority-based approval authorities for transaction costs

evidence.note: Due diligence, legal and tax advisory fees are transaction-related expenses (F2022); outside consultants appear in about 37% of PE deals. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct or co-control deal.

steps.name: Scope legal diligence and instruct external counsel
steps.description: In-house legal counsel agrees the legal diligence scope and materiality thresholds with the deal team, instructs the external law firm and asks it to start the purchase agreement markup.

evidence.note: Round 2 includes the draft definitive agreement. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct or co-control deal.

steps.name: Review data room and log questions
steps.description: The associate reads the information memorandum, financial statements, customer and supplier contracts and management accounts in the virtual data room, notes gaps and inconsistencies and builds the question list.

error.defect_description: A material contract term or one-off item is missed.

evidence.note: Data room review is the core of second-round diligence. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct or co-control deal.

steps.name: Submit questions and chase answers
steps.description: The analyst loads the questions into the data room Q&A module by workstream, tracks open items in a spreadsheet and chases the seller's adviser for overdue answers.

evidence.note: Q&A and follow-ups are part of round 2. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct or co-control deal.

steps.name: Wait for seller answers and added documents
steps.description: The seller's banker and management answer questions in batches and upload added documents to the data room. Sometimes the seller pauses or narrows the field.

next.condition: seller drops the team or pulls the process

evidence.note: Seller response cadence is the author's estimate within a 4-6 week round 2.

steps.name: Attend management presentation and site visit
steps.description: The principal and director attend the management presentation, tour a main site and test management's plan, then write up notes and new questions for the team.

evidence.note: Management presentations and site visits in stage 2. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct or co-control deal.

steps.name: Build operating model and returns analysis
steps.description: The associate builds the operating model from management accounts and the data room, adds the capital structure, exit cases and sensitivities, and compares trading and transaction multiples pulled from market data.

error.defect_description: Formula or assumption error, for example wrong working-capital or tax treatment.

evidence.note: Financial modelling and valuation are core associate duties. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct or co-control deal.

steps.name: Review model and challenge assumptions
steps.description: The principal walks through the model with the associate, challenges growth, margin and exit assumptions against diligence findings and comparables, and lists changes.

evidence.note: Review loop share is the author's estimate. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct or co-control deal.

steps.name: Assess operations and draft value creation plan
steps.description: A Portfolio Value Creation principal reviews operations, management capability and digital opportunities, and drafts the first value creation plan and the governance rights the fund should seek.

evidence.note: PVC assists in due diligence (F2021); operating partners join pre-deal work in about 45% of PE deals. Low end covers passive minority deals. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct or co-control deal.

steps.name: Receive advisers' draft reports
steps.description: The accounting firm sends its quality of earnings and net debt findings, the strategy consultant its market report, the law firm its red-flag legal report and, where relevant, the environmental firm its Phase I report.

evidence.note: Commercial work can have two weeks or less; Phase I assessment under ASTM E1527-21. Wait is the remaining time after earlier steps.

steps.name: Review draft diligence reports and update the model
steps.description: The senior associate reads each report, lists red flags and quantified adjustments to earnings and net debt, agrees follow-ups with the advisers and updates the model and price range.

error.defect_description: An adviser adjustment is carried into the model with the wrong sign or period.

evidence.note: Confirmatory findings feed price and terms. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct or co-control deal.

steps.name: Decide whether to continue after confirmatory findings
steps.description: The group head meets the team, reviews red flags, the updated value range and the competitive position, and decides whether to keep spending on the deal.

next.condition: red flag or value gap, team withdraws
re-run the case on new assumptions
seller signals the team is out

evidence.note: Funnel: 13.6 of 23.7 deep-diligence deals reach a signed LOI and 6.1 close; branch shares are the author's split for the stage before the final bid.

steps.name: Prepare term sheet and send it to Tax and Sustainable Investing
steps.description: The senior associate writes the proposed structure, price, governance rights and jurisdictions into a term sheet and sends it to the tax and sustainable investing teams for their reviews.

evidence.note: Tax and ESG inputs required for committee memos. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct or co-control deal.

steps.name: Negotiate governance and co-investment terms with partners
steps.description: The group head negotiates board seats, vetoes, information rights and co-investment allocation with the lead sponsor or co-investors, and agrees how the consortium will bid.

evidence.note: DPE makes sizable investments alongside aligned partners. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct or co-control deal.

steps.name: Mark up purchase agreement and review legal findings
steps.description: Legal counsel reviews the external firm's legal report, settles the purchase agreement markup and the shareholder agreement term sheet for the final bid, and flags issues for the memo.

control.basis: Legal department review of transaction documents before a binding offer

evidence.note: Final bids are submitted with a markup of the definitive agreement. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct or co-control deal.

steps.name: Confirm financing and warranty insurance terms
steps.description: The principal confirms acquisition debt terms with the lead sponsor or lenders and, where used, obtains the buy-side warranty insurance quote through the broker, and adds both to the model.

evidence.note: RWI quotes in 2-4 business days, underwriting 1-2 weeks. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct or co-control deal.

steps.name: Integrate tax structure memo and ESG and climate assessment
steps.description: The associate waits for the tax structure memo and the sustainable investing assessment, adds withholding and structure costs to the model and inserts the ESG and climate scenario findings into the memo draft.

control.basis: Climate Change Security Selection Framework for material transactions

evidence.note: Climate Change Security Selection Framework applies to material transactions needing senior-most committee approval (F2022). Wait for the other teams is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Set valuation range and bid price
steps.description: The director reviews the final model, returns against the hurdle for the strategy, sensitivities and the competitive picture, and sets the recommended price and walk-away level.

evidence.note: Pricing judgment before final proposals. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct or co-control deal.

steps.name: Draft investment memo
steps.description: The senior associate and associate write the investment memo: thesis, business and market, diligence findings, value creation plan, valuation and returns, risks and mitigants, tax, ESG, governance and the requested approval.

error.defect_description: Figures in the memo do not match the final model, or a section is missing.

evidence.note: Associates present new opportunities at investment committee meetings. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct or co-control deal.

steps.name: Review and edit the memo
steps.description: The director reads the draft, checks key numbers against the model, rewrites the thesis and risk sections and sends it back with comments or passes it to the group head.

evidence.note: Memo review loops are common practice; shares and times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review memo with the group head
steps.description: The group head reads the memo, tests the thesis and price with the team and decides whether to take it to the department review.

evidence.note: Group-level review under the approval authorities; shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check approval authority and required sign-offs
steps.description: A business management associate checks the deal size against the Investment Management Authorities to confirm the approving body, and checks that tax, legal, ESG and risk sections and sign-offs are present.

control.basis: Investment Management Authorities set by the CEO: transaction approval authorities

evidence.note: Investment Management Authorities set approval authorities by size. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct or co-control deal.

steps.name: Present at the department investment review
steps.description: The deal team presents to the department head and group heads at the weekly department review, answers questions and records the endorsement or required changes before the item goes to the Portfolio Execution Committee.

control.basis: Investment Management Authorities: department-level committee review

evidence.note: Department decision committees approve or endorse transactions by size. Meeting cadence and shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Submit memo to Risk and the committee secretariat
steps.description: The associate files the final memo, model and appendices in the memo repository and sends them to the risk team and the Portfolio Execution Committee secretariat for the next agenda.

evidence.note: PEC reviews new investments with risk input. Times are the author's estimates for a mid-sized direct or co-control deal.

exceptions.name: Red flag or value gap in confirmatory diligence
exceptions.description: Adviser reports reveal an earnings, legal or environmental issue, or the price needed to win is above the team's value; the group head stops spending.

exceptions.name: Seller drops the team or pulls the process
exceptions.description: The seller narrows the field, signals the bid is out of range or suspends the sale.

exceptions.name: Model rework after review
exceptions.description: The principal sends the model back for changes to growth, margin, structure or exit assumptions.

exceptions.name: Memo rewrite
exceptions.description: The director or group head returns the memo for rewrites of thesis, numbers or risk sections.

exceptions.name: Missing sign-off or wrong approval tier
exceptions.description: The authority check finds a missing tax, legal or ESG section or the wrong approving body.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from screening approval to memo submitted or deal dropped
benchmarks.population: Large institutional investors in second-round private company auctions

evidence.note: Round 2 runs 4-6 weeks and negotiations 6-8 weeks (Wall Street Prep); about four to five months from launch to signing (Macabacus). The p50 and p90 are the author's reading for the buyer's phase 2 work.

benchmarks.unit: share of deep-diligence deals that close
benchmarks.population: 71 PE firms answering the funnel question in a survey of 79 firms

evidence.note: 6.1 closes per 23.7 deals in deep diligence.

benchmarks.population: Hundreds of transactions on the Intralinks data room platform

evidence.note: Average for private-target deals; 203 days across all deals.

benchmarks.unit: days or less between data room access and decision

evidence.note: Stated as two weeks or less.

benchmarks.unit: share of deals using outside consultants pre-deal

evidence.note: Table 24.

pain_points.description: Seller timetables leave little time for commercial and financial work, so teams bid on draft adviser findings.

evidence.note: Two weeks or less between data room access and decision.

pain_points.description: Deal teams spend heavily on deals they do not win: roughly three in four deep-diligence deals never close, and adviser fees are sunk.

evidence.note: Funnel 23.7 to 6.1.

pain_points.description: The memo waits on tax, sustainability and legal inputs from other teams that work several deals at once.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from the separate tax and ESG processes in the process map.

pain_points.description: Several layers of memo review (director, group head, authority check, department review) add days and rewrites before the committee sees the deal.

evidence.note: Layered approval authorities; review loop shares are estimates.

assumptions: The process starts when the group head accepts a screening memo and ends at memo submission; the first-round bid, risk review, committee approval and closing negotiations are other processes.

Volume follows the process map (28 deals a month entering deep diligence). This looks high for direct private equity alone: the DPE portfolio held 88 investments in F2021 with C$3.5 billion of new investment, which suggests far fewer than 7 closings a month. The volume may include co-investments and Asia direct deals.

Branch shares are set so that about 55% of deals reach a memo, 35% are dropped by the team and 9% are lost in the auction, consistent with the published funnel (95% of deep-diligence deals offer terms, 57% sign an LOI, 26% close).
All deals are treated as requiring Portfolio Execution Committee approval; small deals within department authority would stop at the department review.

Hands-on times count focused work only; deal teams also spend many unrecorded hours in calls and travel. At the process map volume the simulated hands-on time implies about 47 FTE, and the roles state 45 FTE, which is close to half of the roughly 95 people in the direct and Asia private equity groups. This is another sign that the process map volume is high.

The simulated median (about 54 days) is above the 45-day benchmark reading because deals that are dropped usually fall out only after the adviser reports arrive, late in the phase; the benchmark itself is a tier B reading of practitioner stage lengths, not a measured statistic.
Loaded costs per hour come from the organisation file (total compensation scaled to F2022 personnel expense, times overhead factor 1.25, divided by 1,950 hours).

pe_smd, pe_bm, legal_counsel and compliance_officer are organisation roles that the process map does not list for this process; they are added because the department review, authority check, legal markup and watch-list steps need them.
